docs.title: pid4cat Documentation
docs.text:
pid4cat is a persistent identifier (PID) service designed and operated by NFDI4Cat for the catalysis research community. The pid4cat service builds upon existing PID infrastructure (Handle System) while providing enhanced capabilities for metadata management and namespace delegation. It enables partner organizations to manage their own sub-namespaces while maintaining a consistent approach to PID metadata management via a LinkML-based model.

The pid4cat registry is in final pre-production testing.

The production launch is planned for Q1 2027. Organizations interested in becoming an SNAA can contact HLRS now.

  • Overview on pid4cat identifiers
  • Schema documentation for the metadata model
  • Versioning of the model and how schema changes are signalled

The pid4cat documentation and model are developed on GitHub at NFDI4Cat/pid4cat-model.

docs.title: Benefits of using pid4cat
docs.text:
• Distributed management: Partner organizations can manage their own namespaces
  • Rich metadata: Support for comprehensive, structured identifier-related metadata
  • Interoperability: Compatible with existing PID systems and linked data principles.
  • Community standards: Alignment with catalysis research community standards and practices

docs.title: REST APIs
docs.text:
Two APIs give access to pid4cat handles:

  • The pid4cat registry API creates and changes PIDs. Only namespace owners (SNAAs) can use it.
  • The Handle.net API returns the current handle record of any PID. It is public and read-only.

docs.title: pid4cat registry API
docs.text:
The registry is in pre-production testing.

URLs and behaviour may change until the service is launched.

The registry is the reference for its own API: Swagger UI to try requests, ReDoc with full-text search, and the OpenAPI specification as YAML or JSON. This section gives an overview.

The base URL is https://pid.nfdi4cat.org/api/v1. A PID <prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix> (see Structure of pid4cat handles) has the path

https://pid.nfdi4cat.org/api/v1/pids/<prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix>

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Each namespace owner receives an API key from the pid4cat administrators. The API key is exchanged for short-lived tokens:

  1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with {"api_key": "…"} returns an access_token, a refresh_token and the lifetime of the access token in seconds (expires_in).
  2. Every request sends the access token in the header Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.
  3. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with {"refresh_token": "…"} returns a new token pair. A refresh token works only once.

docs.title: Creating a PID
docs.text:
The namespace owner chooses the <id-suffix> and creates the PID with a POST to its path:

POST https://pid.nfdi4cat.org/api/v1/pids/<prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix>
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "landing_page_url": "https://example.org/samples/s-001",
  "status": "REGISTERED",
  "curation_contact": "pid-curator@example.org",
  "resource_info": {
    "resource_category": "SAMPLE",
    "representation_variants": []
  }
}

The fields follow the pid4cat metadata model. A PID that already exists gets the status 409.

docs.title: PID states
docs.text:
State Meaning On the Handle server SUBMITTED Reserved; not yet linked to a resource Not present REGISTERED Linked to a resource Resolves to the landing page DEPRECATED Deprecated, for example because the resource can no longer be found Kept, with status DEPRECATED OBSOLETED Obsolete, for example because another PID replaces it, or deleted Kept if the PID was ever REGISTERED

A new PID is SUBMITTED unless the request sets "status": "REGISTERED" and gives a landing page. POST …/activate registers a SUBMITTED PID. DEPRECATED and OBSOLETED are final.

docs.title: Changing a PID
docs.text: Each part of the metadata has its own path below the PID, for example …/landing-page, …/contact, …/resource-info and …/relations. GET reads the part, PUT replaces it, and POST …/relations adds one relation. The <id-suffix> of a PID cannot be changed.

docs.title: Test namespaces
docs.text: Each namespace <ns-suffix> has a test namespace test-<ns-suffix>. Its PIDs are registered on a separate test Handle server, so an integration can be tried out without creating real PIDs.

docs.title: Handle.net API
docs.text:
The HDL.NET Proxy Server System returns the handle record of every pid4cat PID on the Handle server. It needs no authentication.

GET https://hdl.handle.net/api/handles/<prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix>

Response:

{
  "responseCode": 1,
  "handle": "<prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix>",
  "values": [
    {
      "index": 1,
      "type": "URL",
      "data": {
        "format": "string",
        "value": "https://example.org/resource"
      },
      "ttl": 86400,
      "timestamp": "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    // Additional handle values containing metadata
  ]
}

The query parameter noredirect shows the handle record as an HTML table, for example

  • https://hdl.handle.net/21.11165/4cat/d4y/sample-001?noredirect

The Jupyter notebook examples/hdl-net-api-demo.ipynb reads pid4cat records with the pid4cat_model.handle_api module of the pid4cat-model package.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
To use pid4cat services, an organization applies to HLRS to become a Sub-Name Assigning Authority (SNAA). The requirements are listed in Registration as SNAA.

Upon approval, the organization will receive:

  • A unique namespace suffix (<ns-suffix>)
  • An API key for the pid4cat registry API
  • Documentation and support for the integration into SNAA-operated services

docs.title: Structure of pid4cat handles
docs.text:
A pid4cat handle has the form <prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix>, for example 21.11165/4cat/d4y/sample-001:

  • <prefix>: the Handle prefix.
  • 4cat: a fixed segment that marks pid4cat handles.
  • <ns-suffix>: the namespace of one SNAA, assigned at registration. It has three lower-case characters from the Crockford Base32 alphabet (digits and letters without i, l, o and u): a letter, a digit, then a letter or digit, for example d4y. Some combinations are reserved and never assigned. Test namespaces have the form test-<ns-suffix>.
  • <id-suffix>: the identifier within the namespace. It has 1 to 36 characters from a-z, 0-9, . and -. It contains no /, so every pid4cat handle has exactly four segments.

Handles resolve case-insensitively. Lower case in <ns-suffix> and <id-suffix> gives each handle a single spelling.

docs.title: Creating and updating identifiers
docs.text:
SNAAs create and update PIDs with the pid4cat registry API. The SNAA chooses the <id-suffix> of each PID following its own naming conventions. A PID is created with a POST request to its path, for example:

POST https://pid.nfdi4cat.org/api/v1/pids/21.11165/4cat/d4y/sample-001

The request body contains the landing page URL and the metadata required by the pid4cat-model. Later requests can change the landing page URL and the metadata, but not the <id-suffix>. The test namespace test-<ns-suffix> allows trying this out without creating real PIDs.

docs.title: Resolving identifiers
docs.text:
pid4cat identifiers can be resolved using:

  1. Handle System proxy (preferred): https://hdl.handle.net/<prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix>
  2. pid4cat resolver: https://handle.nfdi4cat.org/<prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix>
  3. DOI proxy: https://doi.org/<prefix>/4cat/<ns-suffix>/<id-suffix>; the DOI resolver also resolves handles other than DOIs.

Resolution redirects to the landing page of the identified resource, which the responsible SNAA maintains.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
pid4cat handles store their metadata directly in the handle record, as ePIC handles do. DOI metadata, in contrast, are managed by DOI providers such as DataCite in separate systems.

The metadata describe the PID and its relations to other PIDs. Relations to relevant existing PIDs should be given when the PID is created; relations that come into existence later may be added, but this is not required.

The metadata schema is defined in the Linked Data Modeling Language (LinkML) and documented in Schema. The Python package derived from the schema is described in Tools and Services.

docs.title: Core Metadata Elements
docs.text:
pid4cat requires a set of core metadata elements for each identifier:

Element Description Required URL Landing page URL Yes EMAIL Contact email of PID curator in responsible SNAA Yes STATUS PID status information Yes SCHEMA_VER The version of the pid4cat metadata model Yes METADATA_LICENSE SPDX license specifier "CC0-1.0" Yes RESOURCE Information about the resource and its representation (json) Yes RELATED Information about related identifiers and the type of relation (json) No CHANGES Structured change log for the PID record (json) Yes

These metadata elements are stored in the handle records of pid4cat PIDs.

docs.title: Permanent URIs for the metadata schema
docs.text:
All elements in the schema (classes, slots, enums) have w3id.org-URIs. These point to the latest schema version released.For example: https://w3id.org/nfdi4cat/pid4cat-model/class/HandleRecord is redirected to https://nfdi4cat.github.io/pid4cat-model/latest/elements/classes/HandleRecord/.

Schema elements from older releases can also be referenced via permanent URIs. For example, to reference the same class but from Release 0.4.0, just insert the release tag into the URI: https://w3id.org/nfdi4cat/pid4cat-model/v0.4.0/class/HandleRecord

The full LinkML schema in YAML format can be downloaded from https://w3id.org/nfdi4cat/pid4cat-model/ when specifying the media type application/yaml.

Example download command for httpie:

http -o pid4cat_model.yaml --download https://w3id.org/nfdi4cat/pid4cat-model Accept:"application/yaml"

for curl:

curl -o pid4cat_model.yaml -L -H "accept:application/yaml" https://w3id.org/nfdi4cat/pid4cat-model

docs.title: Metadata Validation
docs.text: The pid4cat registry validates all metadata against the pid4cat-model schema. A request with invalid metadata is rejected with an error message for each problem.

docs.title: Metadata Access
docs.text: pid4cat metadata can be read with the pid4cat registry API and, for PIDs on the Handle server, publicly with the Handle.net API. All metadata is provided under the CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, enabling unrestricted reuse.

docs.title: Open Data
docs.text: All pid4cat metadata is published under the CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication. The handle record of every pid4cat PID on the Handle server, including its metadata, can be read without authentication through the Handle.net API.

docs.title: PID Graph integration
docs.text:
The PID Graph connects persistent identifiers of different types into a network of scientific and scholarly entities. pid4cat contributes to it by:

  1. Recording relations to other PIDs in its metadata
  2. Using relation types adapted from the DataCite metadata schema
  3. Exposing metadata in machine-readable formats
  4. Linking resource categories and relation types to concepts of the Voc4Cat vocabulary

docs.title: What is a Persistent Identifier and what is pid4cat?
docs.text:
A Persistent Identifier (PID) is a long-lasting reference to a digital resource that remains valid regardless of changes in the resource's location or ownership.

pid4cat is a PID service for the catalysis research community, built on the Handle System. It consists of three main components:

  1. pid4cat-model: A data model for metadata of persistent identifiers
  2. pid4cat registry: A service with a REST API for creating, updating, and retrieving PIDs and their associated metadata
  3. pid4cat hosting: Operation of a production handle system with an officially registered permanent handle-prefix 21.11165 and of an analogous test system with the demo prefix 21.T11978.

docs.title: Design goals
docs.text:
For the PID system:

  • Provide PIDs for NFDI4Cat and its tools & services
  • Low cost per PID
  • Managed and operated by one main authority (HLRS)
  • Sub ID-spaces for sub name assigning authorities (SNAA)
  • Allow each SNAA to create IDs according to self-defined patterns (with some constraints on allowed characters)
  • Custom REST-API access with authorization for PID-management by SNAAs
  • Use of a single common handle prefix
  • Open tools & open data (CC-0 for PID metadata, MIT or Apache-2-license for code)

For the PID metadata model:

  • Predominantly metadata about the PID (status, changes, contact)
  • Low post-creation update work for metadata
  • Minimum information about the resource
  • What is identified? (selection among few types)
  • How to access the resource? (for example which other media type than html can be requested)
  • Relations to other PIDs (reuse relations from DataCite metadata schema)
  • linked-data conform to facilitate PID-graph integration/creation

For the pid4cat pattern:

  • Recognizable as pid4cat
  • Short meaningless identifier for the namespaces of SNAAs.
  • Best-practice guidelines for identifier patterns to help the SNAAs.
  • Within the prefix space, only the combination of identifier for the namespace and SNAA-created ID must be unique to allow offline (uncoordinated & de-centralized) minting of identifiers.

docs.title: Handle System Basics
docs.text:
Every handle consists of two parts: its naming authority, otherwise known as its prefix, and a unique local name under the naming authority, otherwise known as its suffix:1

<Handle> ::= <Handle Naming Authority> "/" <Handle Local Name>

The naming authority and local name are separated by the ASCII character "/".

21.zzzzz/4cat/638s-k9dx
\______/\_____________/
   |           |
 prefix      suffix

The collection of local names under a naming authority defines the local handle namespace for that naming authority. Any local name must be unique under its local namespace. The uniqueness of a naming authority and a local name under that authority ensures that any handle is globally unique within the context of the Handle System.

HLRS administers the pid4cat prefixes. pid4cat handles resolve through the Handle System proxy, the DOI proxy and the pid4cat resolver; see Resolving identifiers.

docs.title: Identifier pattern
docs.text:
The handle-suffix part has to fulfill different roles in pid4cat handles. First, it should allow the minting of PIDs by different institutions. This requires that a part of the PID suffix is used as an identifier for an organization using a sub-PID-namespace. Second, the suffix must contain an identifier part that makes it unique in each sub-PID-namespace. Third, the suffix should make pid4cat handles easily distinguishable from other handles (for humans).

The following scheme was selected for pid4cat handles:

  • <handle-prefix> / <branding-suffix> / <ns-suffix> / <id-suffix>
21.zzzzz/4cat/xxx/723-hk-09
        \___/\__/\________/
          |    |      |
   branding    |     id-suffix
     suffix   ns-suffix

As a branding label we use 4cat to make pid4cat handles easily distinguishable.4 This has already been implemented for NFDI4Cat's data repository. Next comes an identifier ns-suffix for the namespace of sub-authorities associated with the PID-subspace followed by the ID-suffix part. Regarding uniqueness, it is important to note that only the combination of ns-suffix and id-suffix must be unique. Due to this all SNAAs are independent in the IDs they generate. The same id-suffix may be present in different sub namespaces. The different parts are separated by the ASCII character "/".

Rules for the <ns-suffix>:

  • The ns-suffix is short and opaque; its exact format is given in Structure of pid4cat handles.
  • Sub-namespaces have to be requested at HLRS.
  • The ns-suffixes are generated randomly and have no meaning (for example they do not match abbreviations of institutions).2

Rules for the <id-suffix>:

  • The local IDs are managed by the responsible SNAA. They may contain lower-case letters [a-z], numbers [0-9] and the symbols [.-].
  • The local IDs have at most 36 characters including dashes (the length of a UUID).
  • If an optional checksum is included, it must be calculated including the <ns-suffix> and ignoring dashes.

Case-sensitivity:

  • The <ns-suffix> and <id-suffix> part of pid4cat PIDs are case insensitive.3
  • pid4cat PIDs are written in lower case, see display guidelines.
  • Checksums, if used, are case-insensitive; their check characters are written in lower case like the rest of the PID.

Suggested checksum calculations:

  • The ISO 7064 Mod 97, 10 algorithm. It evaluates the whole identifier as an integer which is valid if the number modulo 97 is 1. It has two check digits and is easy to compute. Strings may be handled by replacing the letters with a number, e.g. its ascii-code, before applying the algorithm. It is for example used by ROR and DataCite.
  • The ISO 7064 Mod 37, 36 algorithm. It uses one alphanumeric check digit and the identifier itself may also be alphanumeric (digit or char). Hence, it is well suited to detect error in alphanumeric identification numbers. This algorithm is for example used by the Global Release Identifier.

Implementations of these algorithms are available in many languages, for example python-stdnum and base32-lib for Python or cdigit for JavaScript. We have also added many ISO 7064 checksum algorithms to the pid4cat-model Python package.

docs.title: Use case: PIDs for samples, devices etc.
docs.text:
pid4cat identifiers can be used for various resources in the catalysis research domain (table copied from schema):

Category Definition Description of use COLLECTION voc4cat:0005012 A collection is a group of resources and/or other collections SAMPLE voc4cat:0005013 A representative part of a material of interest on which observations are made. MATERIAL voc4cat:0005014 A material used in the research process (except samples). DEVICE voc4cat:0005015 A physical device used in a research or manufacturing process. DATA_OBJECT voc4cat:0005016 A collection of data available for access or download. A data object might be a data file, a data set, a data collection. DATA_SERVICE voc4cat:0005017 An organized system of operations that provide data processing functions or access to datasets.

The categories are linked to SKOS concepts defined in the Voc4Cat vocabulary. Such mappings to machine-readable terminologies facilitate the use of pid4cat PIDs in linked-data applications and are key to fully realize FAIR data.

docs.title: Use case: repo4cat
docs.text:
Repo4cat is the data sharing portal created and operated by NFDI4Cat. It is built upon Dataverse. Repo4cat makes use of pid4cat handles to persistently identify the stored resources.

Example handle PID for data in the production instance of repo4cat:

  • https://hdl.handle.net/21.11165/4cat/638s-k9dx
  • The shoulder 4cat/ is also used as "PID-namespace" for repo4cat PIDs.
  • The <ns-suffix> is not present in repo4cat PIDs.

Currently the PIDs minted by repo4cat lack the rich metadata that are attached to other pid4cat PIDs due to limitations of Dataverse.

docs.title: Logos & display guidelines
docs.text: The pid4cat identifier should be displayed consistently across all platforms to ensure recognition and proper use.

docs.title: Display Format
docs.text:
When displaying pid4cat identifiers in text:

  • Use the full handle identifier including prefix, branding suffix, namespace suffix, and local identifier part
  • Do not abbreviate any part of the identifier
  • Use the lower-case form of the identifier

Example: 21.11165/4cat/d4y/sample-001

When creating hyperlinks use the handle.net resolver URL:

  • https://hdl.handle.net/21.11165/4cat/d4y/sample-001

For using pid4cat identifiers in linked-data applications we plan to register pid4cat as the preferable prefix for https://hdl.handle.net/21.11165/4cat/ in Semantic Farm (formerly Bioregistry). This allows to use the CURIE (compact URI) notation:

  • pid4cat:d4y/sample-001

docs.title: Logo Usage
docs.text:
When referencing pid4cat in applications, websites, or publications, the following logo guidelines apply:

  • The official pid4cat logo should be used when possible
  • Maintain the aspect ratio of the logo
  • Do not modify or alter the logo
  • Ensure sufficient clear space around the logo

The official pid4cat logos can be downloaded from the docs/images folder of the pid4cat-model repository: logo-with-text.svg for light and logo-with-text-dark.svg for dark backgrounds.

docs.title: Local Identifier Design
docs.text:
SNAAs are encouraged to follow these best practices when designing their local identifier scheme:

  1. Consistency: Adopt a consistent pattern across all identifiers within your namespace
  2. Documentation: Document your identifier pattern for future reference
  3. Avoid semantics: Minimize semantic content that might become outdated.
  4. Semantic identifiers contain meaningful information (e.g., JoeMiller-Sample-LiMg-001)
  5. Opaque identifiers have no inherent meaning (e.g., x7z-9q2)
  6. Validation: Implement validation to ensure identifiers conform to your pattern
  7. Checksums: Consider incorporating checksums for error detection
  8. Future-proofing: Design for scalability and longevity

If the resources that you want to assign identifiers to, have already identifiers in a local system (for example an electronic lab notebook), it is strongly suggested to reuse these locally unique identifiers for the identifier part in the pid4cat identifier. Often these are just integer numbers or type-number combinations.

If you design a new scheme, consider how the IDs are used. For example, whenever reading and typing of the IDs by humans is important, consider using character sets (alphabets) designed for this purpose and/or using a checksum.

  • Base32-encoded sequential number with checksum:

For example, base32-encoding the number "123456789" and appending its ISO 7064 Mod 97-10 checksum "78", as base32-lib does, gives the ID:

3nq-k8n-78

For pure machine use and if global uniqueness is important consider using

  • UUID4-based identifiers (unordered):
40944082-40ed-4f66-9e8f-66fbcd3908a9
  • UUID7-based identifiers (time-ordered):
0195c559-4b8a-7201-a7ab-f1a5d06687e0

See also suffix design in identifier pattern section and PID literature4,5.

docs.title: Governance
docs.text:
pid4cat is governed by a two-tiered structure:

  1. pid4cat Core Organization: Responsible for the overall governance, technical operation, and sustainability of the pid4cat service
  2. Sub-Name Assigning Authorities (SNAAs): Partner organizations responsible for managing identifiers within their assigned sub-namespaces

docs.title: Registration as SNAA
docs.text:
To become a Sub-Name Assigning Authority (SNAA), an organization must:

  1. Submit an application to the Core Organization (HLRS)
  2. Demonstrate the capability to maintain identified resources
  3. Agree to the pid4cat policies
  4. Designate technical and administrative contacts

docs.title: Identifier Persistence
docs.text:
pid4cat is committed to the persistence of identifiers. Once created, an identifier should remain resolvable indefinitely. This implies:

  1. No deletion: Identifiers must not be deleted, even if the identified resource is no longer available
  2. Tombstones: If a resource becomes unavailable, a tombstone page should be provided with information about the resource and its status
  3. Responsibility: SNAAs are responsible for maintaining the resolution of identifiers they create

In exceptional circumstances, identifiers may be deleted or transferred, but only with the approval of the pid4cat Core Organization.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
Metadata associated with identifiers can be updated to reflect changes in the resource or to correct errors.

  1. Metadata Quality: SNAAs must provide accurate and complete metadata
  2. Metadata Updates: Metadata may be updated to correct errors or reflect changes in the resource
  3. Core Organization Rights: The Core Organization reserves the right to update metadata to ensure policy compliance
  4. Provenance: All metadata updates are recorded with provenance information
  5. Metadata License: All metadata is made available under CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication

docs.title: Resource Access
docs.text:
pid4cat does not require identified resources to be openly accessible. However:

  1. Landing page requirement: All identifiers must resolve to a landing page with basic metadata about the resource or point directly to the resource.
  2. Access information: If access to the resource is restricted, the landing page must provide information about the restrictions and if/how access can be obtained.
  3. Metadata accessibility: Metadata associated with identifiers is openly accessible, even if the resource itself is not.

docs.title: SNAA Responsibilities
docs.text:
Each SNAA is responsible for:

  1. Identifier Management: Creating and maintaining identifiers within their sub-namespace
  2. Resource Maintenance: Ensuring identified resources remain accessible or providing appropriate tombstone pages
  3. Metadata Accuracy: Providing and maintaining accurate metadata
  4. Policy Compliance: Adhering to all pid4cat policies
  5. Contact Information: Maintaining up-to-date technical and administrative contacts
  6. Sustainability: Contributing to the long-term sustainability of pid4cat

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text:
pid4cat adopts the following licensing policies:

  1. Service licensing: The pid4cat service is operated under [specific license]
  2. Metadata licensing:
  3. Metadata submitted to pid4cat is made available under the CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication
  4. This allows for unrestricted reuse of metadata, promoting interoperability and discovery
  5. Resource licensing:
  6. pid4cat does not mandate specific licenses for identified resources
  7. SNAAs should state the license of the resource on its landing page
  8. Recommended licenses include Creative Commons licenses, Open Data Commons licenses, and other open licenses

docs.title: Sustainability
docs.text:
To ensure the long-term sustainability of the pid4cat service:

  1. Succession planning: The pid4cat Core Organization has established succession plans to ensure continuity of service
  2. SNAA succession: SNAAs must designate a successor organization or return control of their sub-namespace to the Core Organization if they can no longer fulfill their responsibilities
  3. Financial model: [Details about the financial model supporting pid4cat]
  4. Data preservation: All identifier metadata is regularly backed up and preserved in multiple locations

docs.title: pid4cat-model Python package
docs.text:
pid4cat-model is a Python package for

  • reading pid4cat records from the Handle.net API (module pid4cat_model.handle_api).
  • validating pid4cat metadata against the pid4cat-model schema.
  • calculating and validating ISO 7064 checksums which may be used in local identifier schemes.

ISO/IEC 7064 describes eight generic check digit (character) systems for numeric, alphabetic, and alphanumeric strings. It specifies two types of systems that use the same algorithm with different parameters: Pure systems and Hybrid systems.

Algorithm Function name Input string Check character(s) Pure ISO/IEC 7064, MOD 11-2 mod11_2 Numeric (0-9) 1 digit or 'x' (0-9x) ISO/IEC 7064, MOD 37-2 mod37_2 Alphanumeric (0-9a-z) 1 digit, letter, or '*' (0-9a-z*) ISO/IEC 7064, MOD 97-10 mod97_10 Numeric (0-9) 2 digits (0-9) ISO/IEC 7064, MOD 661-26 mod661_26 Alphabetic (a-z) 2 letters (a-z) ISO/IEC 7064, MOD 1271-36 mod1271_36 Alphanumeric (0-9a-z) 2 digits or letters (0-9a-z) Hybrid ISO/IEC 7064, MOD 11,10 mod11_10 Numeric (0-9) 1 digit (0-9) ISO/IEC 7064, MOD 27,26 mod27_26 Alphabetic (a-z) 1 letter (a-z) ISO/IEC 7064, MOD 37,36 mod37_36 Alphanumeric (0-9a-z) 1 digit or letter (0-9a-z)

The pid4cat_model.iso7064 module contains implementations of all algorithms in the table. They accept letters in either case and return check characters in lower case.

docs.title: pid4cat registry
docs.text:
The pid4cat registry is the service with which SNAAs create and manage the PIDs in their namespaces. It authenticates the SNAAs, validates PIDs and their metadata against the pid4cat-model, and registers the PIDs on the Handle server. Its main features are:

  • Create, read, update and state changes of PIDs in the SNAA's namespaces
  • Test namespaces on a separate test Handle server
  • Search across the PIDs a user can access
  • Periodic checks that landing pages and representation variants are reachable
  • A status dashboard

The source code is not yet published. It will be released in 2027 under Apache 2.0 licence. For usage, see pid4cat registry API.

docs.text: LinkML generators derive other representations from the pid4cat-model, for example JSON Schema, SHACL shapes, SQL and code for programming languages other than Python. They are in the /project folder of the repository.

docs.title: Versioning of the pid4cat-model
docs.text:
The versioning of the pid4cat-model is following the SchemaVer scheme proposed in a snowplow blog post. The same principles are applied for the HCA schema versioning. SchemaVer is also adapted by openlineage.

SchemaVer: Given a version number MODEL.REVISION.ADDITION, increment the

  • MODEL when you make a breaking schema change which will prevent interaction with any historical data
  • REVISION when you make a schema change which may prevent interaction with some historical data
  • ADDITION when you make a schema change that is compatible with all historical data

docs.title: Schema version and package version
docs.text:
The schema version is set in the version of the schema file pid4cat_model.yaml and changes only when the schema changes. pid4cat records state the schema version they follow in schema_version (handle record type SCHEMA_VER) with a leading "v", for example "v0.4.3". The Python package provides it as pid4cat_model.SCHEMA_VERSION. CI fails when the schema differs from that of the newest release while its version is unchanged. Formatting, comments and documentation-only fields (description, comments, notes, todos, examples, see_also, title) do not count; for a description change that alters the meaning of an element, raise the version by hand. The same check runs as pre-commit hook check-schema-version on commits that change the schema; it needs the release tags in the clone (git fetch --tags).

The version of the Python package pid4cat-model has four parts, MODEL.REVISION.ADDITION.N (PEP 440): the first three parts are the schema version, and N numbers the releases for that schema, starting at 1. For example, package 0.5.0.1 is the first release of schema version 0.5.0, and 0.5.0.2 the next release with changes to code, dependencies or documentation only.

Releases up to 0.4.3 had three-part package versions. Releases 0.4.0 to 0.4.2 changed code only; their schema is the same as schema version 0.4.3.

The Python classes in pid4cat_model.datamodel are generated from the schema with LinkML. The LinkML version used for a release is pinned in uv.lock at its tag.

docs.title: Releases and documentation
docs.text:
The versions are tagged in git with the package version (for example "v1.2.3.1"), pre-releases with the suffix "rc" and a number (for example "v1.2.3.1rc1"). Based on the tags we also create GitHub releases to provide easy access to all versions and to document the changes between versions. The release workflows refuse a tag that is not the schema version followed by a release number.

Each release gets its own documentation, named like its tag. The schema version ("v1.2.3") is an alias of the documentation of its newest release, and the w3id.org URIs of a schema version redirect to it. Pre-releases do not get this alias.

docs.title: pid4cat-model
docs.text:
A LinkML model for persistent identifiers for resources in catalysis (pid4cat). pid4cat are handle based persistent identifiers (PIDs) for digital or physical resources used in the catalysis research process. PID-related metadata besides the obligatory landing page URL are stored directly in the handle records. The model describes metadata for the PID itself and how to access the identified resource. It does not describe the resource itself with the exception of the resource category, which is a high-level description of what is identified by the pid4cat handle, e.g. a sample or a device.

URI: https://w3id.org/nfdi4cat/pid4cat-model

Name: pid4cat-model

The landing page is an HTML page (media type text/html); representations in other media types are listed in representation_variants. media_type The media type of the representation as defined by IANA metadata_license The license of the metadata of the pid4cat record. The license is set to "CC0-1.0" by default. name The name of the agent that created or modified the PID record. orcid The ORCID of the person permissions The administrator's permissions as a bit mask of 12 flags. related_identifier The related identifier. related_identifiers The related identifiers for the pid4cat record. docs.title: pid4cat-model
docs.text:
A LinkML model for persistent identifiers for resources in catalysis (pid4cat). pid4cat are handle based persistent identifiers (PIDs) for digital or physical resources used in the catalysis research process. PID-related metadata besides the obligatory landing page URL are stored directly in the handle records. The model describes metadata for the PID itself and how to access the identified resource. It does not describe the resource itself with the exception of the resource category, which is a high-level description of what is identified by the pid4cat handle, e.g. a sample or a device.

URI: https://w3id.org/nfdi4cat/pid4cat-model
